title: Ala Singh Offers Thanks and Gifts to the Khalsa

blocks.text: After the battle, Ala Singh comes not as a patron above the Panth but as a beneficiary before it. From a distance he spots the Khalsa emblems, bows with folded hands, and performs the etiquette of reverence before the Singhs who preserved his position.

The thanksgiving is expressed materially as well as verbally. He touches the feet of Nihang Singhs, offers food and money, says Waheguru ji ki Fateh, and Many a horse did he present as gifts to Singhs in acknowledgment of the rescue.
The page turns victory into relationship. Military aid is answered by public gratitude, gift exchange, and renewed recognition of Khalsa authority.
